content.text: Why
That email
It seems like they’re hesitating

I know that they are using individuals from all the Ilitch companies so they said they had enough. Emily mentioned that other opportunities would be coming up which makes me think they’re saving marketing people for that. Emily mentioned that we were trying to find other ways to make money and they reached out to universities for us to sell corporate sponsorship for them? So I feel like they are trying to make us more agency like so we can make money
They mentioned doing that with the creative service team before two. Take on outside design clients. Because we have enough people to do our current jobs ...
So like
Do design for others
Yeah, that hasn’t been brought up in awhile but it sounds like they are trying it with corporate sponsorship first?
So, essentially, they’d sell a sponsorship to Concordia and then as part of that, you’d have to do stuff for them
That’s what is sounds like. Emily mentioned it, said it wasn’t a done deal, but they reached out to U of M about it first.
Ah. So for the masks, have people started making them yet?
Apparently the first group is starting Monday. Shift is 5 am - noon. The following Monday, afternoon shifts will start 12-7pm
So what I’m thinking is
Sorry. I’m thinking that I should write something on the masks because if the shifts haven’t started yet and they get bad press for it, maybe it will force them to stop it
Like, it seems kinda fucked up that they’d have to come in and work in this factory ... are there guidelines? Unions usually mandate factory conditions -- especially in a pandemic
And, like, I feel like my job is kinda to look out for that thing, you know?
Yeah, definitely. I can ask around to see who might be still involved. I only know what I’ve heard from others so I apologize for not having many details
No worries. I’m just trying to poke around it more
What about Ilitch Holdings e-mail address, I gotta get ahold of Shawn Platt to ask him questions. He’s their communication guy
Can’t find an email for Shawn. Found this in a recent colleague email
I guess he went back to DeVos
Jamie Langdon, Ilitch Holdings, Inc. Communications, Jamie.Langdon@IlitchHoldings.com
Thank you
I got through to Jamie, sending her questions

Is working at the mask-making facility voluntary or mandatory for employees?In either case, voluntary or mandatory, if an employee decides against working at the mask-making facility, will they be terminated or subject to unpaid furlough? If unpaid furlough, how long?What are the masks for?
Trying to think of questions
Good questions. I wonder if she’ll respond. I know another big concern was single parents that have to figure out childcare or people without cars that needed transportation.
But I think that they were open with individuals expressing their concerns with human resources
Open as in, like, flexible
Yeah. I don’t know how many people went or what the resolution was, but that was mentioned
This is what I came up with lemme know if I missed anything

Is working at the mask-making facility voluntary or mandatory for employees?In either case, voluntary or mandatory, if an employee decides against working at the mask-making facility, will they be terminated or subject to unpaid furlough? If unpaid furlough, how long?What are the masks for?How many employees were chosen to work mask-making shifts and how were they chosen?What is the company’s current policy on working from home during the pandemic? When was it in put in place?If there is a policy in place about employees working from home, does the company feel it is safe to have employees working in a facility?What kind of physical labor will the employees be doing at the facility?What are the company's safety and social distancing guidelines for working at the facility?
